## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga Pācittiya 1 (*Musāvāda*), translated by Bhikkhu Brahmali as "The training rule on lying", is the opening rule of the Pācittiya section of the Theravāda *Vinaya Piṭaka* [SuttaCentral]. The rule establishes that a monastic who intentionally speaks an untruth commits an offense requiring formal confession [SuttaCentral; Collins 1993; Hüsken 1997]. It introduces the first ten pācittiyas, which comprise the *Musāvādavagga* ("chapter on lying") [Collins 1993]. In doctrinal analyses of moral transgression, scholars note that while Pācittiya 1 governs deliberate lying in general (*sampajānamusā bhāsitum*), it is distinguished from Pārājika 4, where a specific, grave category of falsehood—falsely claiming higher superhuman attainments (*uttarimanussadhamma*)—constitutes an offense entailing irreversible expulsion from the Saṅgha [Collins 1993; Hüsken 1997].

The rule corresponds to the first rule of the Bhikkhu Pātimokkha and shares a direct regulatory counterpart for nuns in Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga Pācittiya 97 [SuttaCentral]. Parallels are preserved across the Vinaya traditions of all major early Buddhist schools, including the Prātimokṣa and Vibhaṅga texts of the Sarvāstivāda, Mūlasarvāstivāda, Mahīśāsaka, Mahāsaṅghika, Dharmaguptaka, and Kāśyapīya extant in Chinese, Sanskrit, and Tibetan recensions [SuttaCentral]. SuttaCentral and DharmaNexus both attest to extensive text reuse between Pācittiya 1 and Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga Pārājika 4 (Bu-Vb Pj4), particularly within their word analyses and casuistic formulations (§2.2.1–2.2.11 of Pc1 matching §4.2.1–4.3.121 of Pj4 across more than 64,000 characters) [SuttaCentral; DharmaNexus]. DharmaNexus further records substantial Pali-internal textual parallels with the canonical *Niddesa* literature (notably Mnd 7 and Cnd 22), the Khandhakas (Kd 1, Kd 11, Kd 14, and Kd 15), and the Vinaya commentaries and sub-commentaries (*Samantapāsādikā*, *Kaṅkhāvitaraṇīpurāṇa-ṭīkā*, and *Vajirabuddhi-ṭīkā*), as well as machine-detected cross-language alignments with Jayarakṣita's Sanskrit *Sphuṭārthā Śrīghanācārasaṃgrahaṭīkā* and the Tibetan *Bhikṣuṇīvinayavibhaṅga* [DharmaNexus].
